chunks: And from him (al-Hasan ibn al-Hayy) from Fadala from Ibn Sinan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever performs the Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her) before raising his legs from the obligatory prayer, he will be forgiven, and he begins with the Takbir."

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), specifically the opening Takbir in this context.
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَةَ الزَّهْرَاءِ: The specific dhikr (remembrance) attributed to Fatimah al-Zahra, consisting of specific phrases recited after prayer.
key_terms.يَثْنِيَ رِجْلَيْهِ: Raising the legs/knees from the bowing (ruku') position to stand.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Tasbih Fatimah after the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific ritual of reciting the 'Tasbih of Fatimah' (Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar) immediately after the Taslim of obligatory prayers, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence as a means of spiritual purification. The promise of forgiveness underscores its significance as a daily act of devotion, while the instruction to begin with Takbir aligns with the standard structure of prayer, ensuring continuity between the formal worship and this recommended supplication. This practice is often viewed as a continuation of the Prophet's household's legacy, reinforcing the connection between ritual prayer and personal piety.
